```{python}
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
import quantities as pq
from neo.core import Block, Segment, SpikeTrain
import elephant.unitary_event_analysis as ue
import elephant.conversion as conv
from elephant.spike_train_generation import StationaryPoissonProcess
from viziphant.unitary_event_analysis import plot_ue
np.random.seed(15) # Fix random seed to guarantee fixed output
%matplotlib inline
```

Reproduce the simulation example from Gruen et al. 1999 where wto neurons fire independently with a `base_rate` but there are also conicident events with a lower `conicidence_rate` and a temporal `jitter`.

```{python}
base_rate = 10. * pq.Hz 
coincidence_rate = 0.2 * pq.Hz
t_start = 0 * pq.ms
t_stop = 5000 * pq.ms
jitter = 5 * pq.ms
```

First, generate two independent spike trains

```{python}
base_spiking = StationaryPoissonProcess(base_rate, t_start, t_stop)
base_spikes_i, base_spikes_j = base_spiking.generate_n_spiketrains(2)
```

Then generate the coincident spikes with a given jitter

```{python}
# Dont randomly inject spikes, instead use nonstationarypoissonprocess
coincident_spiking = StationaryPoissonProcess(coincidence_rate, t_start, t_stop)
coincident_spikes_i = coincident_spiking.generate_spiketrain()
coincident_spikes_j = SpikeTrain(
    times=coincident_spikes_i.times + np.random.uniform(-jitter, jitter, len(coincident_spikes_i))*pq.ms,
    t_start = coincident_spikes_i.t_start,
    t_stop = coincident_spikes_i.t_stop
        )
```

Merge the two spike trains

```{python}
spikes_i = base_spikes_i.merge(coincident_spikes_i)
spikes_j = base_spikes_j.merge(coincident_spikes_j)
```

Plot the spikes
```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, sharex=True)
ax[0].eventplot([base_spikes_i.times, base_spikes_j.times])
ax[0].set(title="Base Spikes", yticks=[0, 1], yticklabels=["i", "j"])
ax[1].eventplot([coincident_spikes_i.times, coincident_spikes_j.times])
ax[1].set(title="Coincident Spikes", yticks=[0, 1], yticklabels=["i", "j"])
ax[2].eventplot([spikes_i.times, spikes_j.times])
ax[2].set(title="Merged Spikes", xlabel="Time [ms]", yticks=[0, 1], yticklabels=["i", "j"])
plt.tight_layout()
```

Now, we use this generative model to simulate multiple trials. First, we define a function to generate one trial 
```{python}
def simulate_trial(t_start, t_stop, base_rate, coincidence_rate, jitter):
    base_spiking = StationaryPoissonProcess(base_rate, t_start, t_stop)
    base_spikes_i, base_spikes_j = base_spiking.generate_n_spiketrains(2)
    coincident_spiking = StationaryPoissonProcess(coincidence_rate, t_start, t_stop)
    coincident_spikes_i = coincident_spiking.generate_spiketrain()
    coincident_spikes_j = SpikeTrain(
        times=coincident_spikes_i.times + np.random.uniform(-jitter, jitter, len(coincident_spikes_i))*pq.ms,
        t_start = coincident_spikes_i.t_start,
        t_stop = coincident_spikes_i.t_stop
        )
    spikes_i = base_spikes_i.merge(coincident_spikes_i)
    spikes_j = base_spikes_j.merge(coincident_spikes_j)
    return [spikes_i, spikes_j]
```
Then, we simulate `n_trials`

```{python}
n_trials = 50
trials = []
for i in range(n_trials):
    trials.append(simulate_trial(t_start, t_stop, base_rate, coincidence_rate, jitter))
```

Perform unitary event analysis on the simulated data

```{python}
UE = ue.jointJ_window_analysis( trials, bin_size=5*pq.ms, win_size=100*pq.ms, win_step=10*pq.ms, pattern_hash=[3])
```

Plot the results

```{python}
plot_ue(trials, UE, significance_level=0.05)
```

Now load the real data
:q
```{python}
root = Path.cwd().parent.absolute()
sessions = list((root/"data").glob("ses*"))
ses = sessions[0]
spikes = pd.read_parquet(ses/"flash_spikes.parquet")
stimuli = pd.read_parquet(ses/"flash_stimuli.parquet")
```

Select spikes from one `brain_area`
```{python}
brain_area = "V1"
spikes = spikes[spikes["brain_area"]==brain_area]
```

```{python}
block = Block()
tmin, tmax = 0, 1.0
unit_ids = spikes["unit_id"].unique()[[2,4]]
for t in stimuli["start_time"]:
    seg = Segment()
    segment_spikes = spikes[((t+tmin)<=spikes["spike_time"]) & (spikes["spike_time"]<=(t+tmax))]
    for uid in unit_ids:
        spike_times =  segment_spikes[segment_spikes["unit_id"]==uid]["spike_time"].to_numpy()
        spike_times -= t # compute spike times relative to stimulus
        spike_train = SpikeTrain(spike_times, units="s", t_stop=tmax, t_start=tmin)
        seg.spiketrains.append(spike_train)
    block.segments.append(seg)
```

Extract the trials and run UEA
```{python}
trials = [seg.spiketrains for seg in block.segments]
UE = ue.jointJ_window_analysis( trials, bin_size=10*pq.ms, win_size=100*pq.ms, win_step=10*pq.ms)
```

```{python}
plot_ue(trials, UE, significance_level=0.05)
```
